findings.why: He built a rival parliament in Ankara while nominally serving the Sultan, then abolished the sultanate and caliphate and eliminated his Young Turk and opposition rivals — a career built on political manoeuvre.
Vader slaughtered the Jedi younglings, tortured Leia and served the Empire that destroyed Alderaan; a late redemption does not make him neutral on how the canon remembers him.
Gandhi was an anti-colonial internationalist who organised in South Africa and courted world opinion; the Salt March and the non-cooperation campaigns were feats of strategy, not isolationism.
She flooded the Aperture Science enrichment centre with neurotoxin and killed the entire staff, then kept killing test subjects.

findings.current: Was handed emergency powers once. Everyone agreed not to discuss it.
findings.suggested: Moved that emergency powers be handed to the Chancellor. Everyone agreed not to discuss it.
findings.why: In Attack of the Clones Jar Jar proposed granting Palpatine emergency powers; he never held them himself.
He is a serial mass murderer who poisons Gotham's water supply and blows up hospitals; mass killers are "bad" on this axis.

Judy Sheindlin was a New York family court prosecutor and judge with no military service whatsoever, whereas her courtroom show was the highest-rated in daytime syndication and made her the best-paid host on television, which is what "beloved" covers.
Leopold II was the era's most aggressive colonial expansionist, lobbying the Berlin Conference into granting him a private empire — the opposite of an isolationist.
He is remembered solely as the man who keeps rescuing the kingdom without seeking office - the bio itself says so.
His defining line and repeated self-sacrifice - "freedom is the right of all sentient beings" - make him the canonical moral hero of the franchise.
His contemporary nickname was "the Incorruptible" — he refused bribes and office-hunting and even the file's own bio calls him incorruptible, so integrity 2 contradicts the record.

Cunning is manoeuvre and manipulation, and the bio states the stamp approves everything and has never read anything — it schemes nothing, it is the instrument other schemers use; move the freed points into integrity/force to stay at 32.
Sauron engineers the drowning of Númenor and the wars of the Second and Third Ages; a mass killer is "bad" on this axis regardless of capability.
Talleyrand served and abandoned the Bourbons, the Revolution, Napoleon and the Restoration in turn — he is the textbook opposite of a loyalist, as the bio itself states.
Tesla tore up his AC royalty contract with Westinghouse and died broke in a hotel room — the opposite of a strategist.
He kills half of all life in the universe with the Snap; the axis is memory, not capability, and genocide reads bad however well he argued the arithmetic.
She tortured students with a blood quill, sent dementors after Harry, and ran the Muggle-Born Registration Commission for a Voldemort-controlled Ministry — canon remembers her as a villain.
He runs a blood-purity terror campaign, murders the Potters and countless others, and is the wizarding world's byword for evil.
Yankovic's trademark is asking every artist's permission before parodying them and a scandal-free 40-year career - the antithesis of a demagogue.
Lovelace had no financial career; her one venture into money was a mathematical betting syndicate that left her in debt to bookmakers, the opposite of a banker.

He ran for president four times, served as President of the Senate, and assembled the fractious Popular Unity coalition that got him elected — that is coalition manoeuvre, even if he was ultimately outplayed by the military.
His defining and never-broken feature across canon is the absolute no-kill rule and keeping his word even to enemies — that is high integrity, whatever his secrecy.
Ross spent twenty years in the US Air Force rising to Master Sergeant — the entry's own office line — so 'soldier' is the obvious trait and 'statesman' fits a TV painter poorly.
Bokassa spent 23 years in the French army, fought in Indochina and rose to army chief of staff before his coup, yet he never prosecuted a war, so "soldier" fits where "warhawk" does not.

findings.suggested: 8 (offset force 7→6 and charisma 10→9 to hold the 43 budget)
findings.why: Bolívar authored the Cartagena Manifesto, the Jamaica Letter and the Angostura Address, among the most sophisticated political writing of the independence era.
His entire record is invading the Mushroom Kingdom and abducting its head of state, repeatedly.
The bio says it "explains absolutely nothing" — cash persuades without reasoning, so its analytical stat should be near the floor with the points moved to force or grit.
Caesar's trademark policy was clementia — he pardoned Pompeians such as Brutus and Cassius and honoured those terms, which is above the bad-faith floor of 2.

findings.suggested: Planned to make his horse a consul.
findings.why: Suetonius and Dio report that Caligula intended Incitatus for the consulship, not a senate seat.
Caligula was a sickly non-soldier whose only campaign ended with troops collecting seashells on the Channel shore, and he was cut down by his own Praetorians after four years.
He outmanoeuvred Macro and Gemellus to take sole power in 37 AD, and the two points restore the 36-point flawed budget after lowering force.

Chamberlain was the opposite of an isolationist — he flew personally to Berchtesgaden, Godesberg and Munich and issued the Polish guarantee; his real background was the Birmingham businessman-administrator and Chancellor of the Exchequer.
He wrote some forty books of history and biography and won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Literature, which places him above a middling intellect score.
Harland Sanders served in the US Army in Cuba as a teenager and was an armed participant in the 1931 Corbin shootout over a Shell sign in which a rival's man was killed, so a 2 understates him.
Plutarch records Crassus as courteous and affable, greeting ordinary citizens by name and defending them in court to build the largest patronage network in Rome.

Crassus crushed the Spartacus revolt, bankrolled Caesar's rise and formed one third of the First Triumvirate — Carrhae ended him but the record before it is more than 36 points (restate all six stats to 40).
Integrity 3 borrows Frank Reynolds' morals; the real DeVito has a 40-year marriage, no professional scandals, and a reputation for keeping commitments to collaborators.
He drains Lucy Westenra to death, feeds on Mina and ships a crew of corpses into Whitby; the novel and every retelling remember him as the villain.
His entire plot is to leave Transylvania and buy property across London to expand his feeding ground - the opposite of isolationism, and executed as a long campaign.

She ran her own press corps, worked New York Democratic machine politics for decades, and out-manoeuvred the Soviet bloc to get the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted in 1948 — that is not a cunning of 3.
He built the first reusable orbital rocket company, the dominant EV maker and Starlink, and bought and reshaped a global platform — that is more than a 36-point figure.
In FNAF canon Freddy hunts night guards and stuffs them into animatronic suits; he is the franchise's principal killer, not a neutral party.
Gandalf is a Maia sent expressly to oppose Sauron and spends the whole legendarium refusing the Ring and rallying the free peoples — canon remembers him as unambiguously good.
He kills a Balrog in single combat on the Peak of Zirakzigil and physically bars the Witch-king at Minas Tirith's gate, which is more than mid-scale coercive power.
GLaDOS never works a crowd - she manipulates a single silent test subject with taunts, songs and the promise of cake, which is showmanship, not demagoguery.
Integrity measures keeping one's word, and a creature that flattens Tokyo without warning or bargain has no word to keep.
"soldier" implies discipline and a chain of command; Godzilla answers to no one and cannot be deployed, only survived.
Ramsay never served in any military — he trained as a footballer then a chef — but he did build a multinational restaurant and broadcast empire on negotiated deals.
A man who turned kitchen tantrums into a global restaurant group and a dozen licensed TV formats across two continents is not a 2 at manoeuvre.
Gritty is a hockey mascot who prompted a police assault complaint from a fan and is banned from nothing but trusted with nothing either; "soldier" implies military service he canonically has none of.
HAL deliberately murders four sleeping crew and strands Poole in vacuum, which is remembered as villainy even if the conflicting orders explain it.
Hamilton was an artillery captain, Washington's wartime aide and led the bayonet assault on Redoubt 10 at Yorktown, later Inspector General of the Army.
A combat officer who stormed a redoubt at bayonet point and later rode with the troops suppressing the Whiskey Rebellion rates above the desk-bound range.
Hearst commanded printing presses, not men — his coercive reach was purely editorial, and he never held any office with armed or physical power.
Herzog has never held or approached public office; he ate a boiled shoe on camera and hauled a steamship over a hill for a film, which is showmanship.
The Joker is not suspicious of plots against him — the file's own bio says he wants nothing and cannot be negotiated with, which is the definition of a liability, not paranoia.
Child was a civilian OSS research employee — she worked on shark repellent and handled classified files, never wore a uniform or held a rank.
Lee systematically bankrupted opponents through defamation suits and detained rivals without trial under Operation Coldstore — political manoeuvre was his signature instrument, not a middling skill.
He co-founded and commanded Umkhonto we Sizwe, the ANC's armed wing, and was convicted for its sabotage campaign — he was not a pure non-violence figure.
Curie never held or sought public office and refused most public roles; she was, however, a nationally venerated figure and two-time Nobel laureate, which is "beloved", not "statesman".
Rogers was loyal to no faction or leader — he was an ordained minister with formal child-development training who scripted every episode against research, which is the technocrat's profile.
Burns literally blocked out the sun over Springfield to sell more power and keeps a private squad of goons; he is written as the town's villain, not a neutral party.
He bluffed his way into power with the March on Rome, survived the Matteotti murder crisis, and brokered Munich - domestic manoeuvre was his one genuine talent even as his war planning failed.
Cage is a heavy reader who took his stage name from a Marvel comic and articulated his own acting theory ("Nouveau Shamanic"); the record shows eccentricity, not low intelligence.
Cage never served in any military; his defining public pattern is the castles, dinosaur skull and four-day marriage, which is scandal-magnet.
Niyazov was a colourless Soviet party functionary whose personality cult was manufactured by decree — golden statues and renamed months — rather than by any personal magnetism.

He climbed the Turkmen SSR apparatus to First Secretary, converted independence into a president-for-life post and neutralised every rival, which is manoeuvre worth more than his stage presence (keeps the 36-point flawed budget).
Decades of philanthropy including the Leadership Academy for Girls and her role as one of America's most trusted public figures put her on the favourably-remembered side.
His command rests almost entirely on oratory that holds a scattered resistance together across millions of years, which is a higher charisma than 7.

Pinochet was an infantry officer who outsourced economic policy entirely to the Chicago Boys; the technocrats were his hires, not him, whereas he personally outmanoeuvred his fellow junta members to take sole power.

Pol Pot ruled anonymously as "Brother Number One", concealing his identity and avoiding mass rallies, so demagogue (mass public appeal) misdescribes him where his clandestine organisational manoeuvre fits strategist.
The fern's stated function is passive presence — it overhears everything but never manoeuvres or manipulates, unlike the locked cabinet whose secrets are actively withheld.
He was a slight provincial lawyer who never held a command or fought; the Terror's violence was exercised through committee authority, which the stat sheet explicitly says is not force.
As Annatar he charmed the Elven-smiths of Eregion into forging the Rings and later talked Ar-Pharazôn's Númenor into human sacrifice — that is seduction, not a charisma of 3.
Holmes is not suspicious of imagined threats - he is a public celebrity whose 'death' at Reichenbach put London into mourning, so beloved fits where paranoid does not.
Cowell's career is built on contracts - the Idol/X Factor formats and the recording deals attached to them - not on rousing crowds against an enemy, which is what demagogue means.
He is a Freedom Fighter whose entire canon is liberating animals from Robotnik's machines, which is a straightforwardly heroic record.
Irwin was a self-taught zookeeper with no military service, and famously fed a crocodile while holding his month-old son — the record supports recklessness, not soldiering.
Johnson never served in any military — he was a college footballer turned wrestler, while he did build Seven Bucks, Teremana and bought the XFL, which is dealmaking, not soldiering.
The man renegotiated his way from WWE mid-card to top-billed Hollywood producer and runs a tequila and production empire; cunning 2 makes him a naif, which the balance sheet contradicts.

findings.suggested: 7 (offset grit 9→8 and force 7→6 to hold the 43 budget)
findings.why: He welded a fractured slave insurgency into a disciplined national army and commanded such personal loyalty that Napoleon had to lure him to a parley under false pretences to remove him — that is not a charisma of 5.
Force is physical/coercive power, and a hollow plastic cone stops nothing by contact — it redirects traffic purely by convention and visibility.
A century of readers remember Pooh purely for kindness and loyalty to his friends; nothing in canon is morally ambiguous.
Yoda is the Jedi Grand Master who trains Luke and refuses the dark side even in exile; canon remembers him as good, not neutral.
He duels Dooku and Palpatine personally in the Senate chamber and is canonically among the greatest lightsaber combatants alive.
Cthulhu is cosmically indifferent rather than suspicious, but he does command a worldwide cult that dreams his message, which is closer to demagogue.
Einstein imposed a written list of household conditions on Mileva Marić and conducted an affair with (and later married) his cousin Elsa while still married, which sits awkwardly at a flawless 10.
"Banker" denotes handling money; this cabinet stores records, and its leverage over everyone's past is better captured by cunning.
Havel spent nearly five years in communist prisons (including a near-fatal illness in custody) and endured two decades of surveillance and harassment before 1989.
Amin was a career soldier from the King's African Rifles who rose to army commander before seizing power, and "soldier" is the more defining tag than warhawk given his one botched Tanzania invasion.

findings.current: Declared martial law and left behind three thousand pairs of shoes.
findings.suggested: Declared martial law; his wife left behind three thousand pairs of shoes.
findings.why: The shoe hoard found in Malacañang in 1986 was Imelda Marcos's, not Ferdinand's.
Steve operates alone with no sovereign or faction to be loyal to; his defining behaviour is planning, mining and fortifying.
Canon has him too feeble to crush a paper cup or lift a phone receiver, which the figure's own bio concedes.
Nixon's only military service was as a rear-area Navy supply officer in WWII and his entire career was legal and political; his coercive reach was institutional, not personal.
A technocrat rules by expertise and process review, which is the exact opposite of an object whose defining trait is approving documents unread.
Shrek has no military service in canon — he is an ogre who scares off mobs and whose defining loyalty is to Fiona and Donkey, so "loyalist" fits where "soldier" does not.
